- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends when sentiment is weak; if sentiment turns negative after a peak, adjust forecast to reflect earlier-than-expected decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts volatility in early days of a downtrend; reduce forecast by 1–3% for first 5–7 days of negative sentiment run.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day history as baseline for smoothing forecast deviations.
